content:
The Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) have completed Special Campaign 6.0 through focused cleanliness and office-space improvement activities across their establishments throughout the country. Around 8,000 sites across all branches of DARE–ICAR were cleaned during the campaign.
The activities included record management, digitisation, plantation, environment-friendly practices, citizen-centric practices, scrap disposal, electronic waste management and enhancement of office spaces. More than 13,000 physical and electronic files were weeded out. The campaign generated revenue of over ₹14 lakh and freed more than 4,000 square feet of space.
Officials across institute campuses conducted awareness camps to sensitise people about the importance of cleanliness. Free medical camps were also organised at several campuses. Felicitation of Safai Mitras has also been a continuing practice.
Officials at all levels actively participated in cleanliness activities, both inside office premises and in the surrounding areas of the campuses. Extensive cleaning drives were carried out in farms, fields and roads surrounding the campuses. Particular attention was given to keeping metal and plastic waste separate from general waste, thereby improving cleanliness.
Special Campaign 6.0 promoted responsible waste management and cleanliness around workplaces. The cleanliness achievements under the campaign exceeded the targets set.

title: Minister of State for Commerce and Industry, Shri Jitin Prasada, Visits Hungary to Strengthen Bilateral Cooperation in Trade, Investment and Technology
subtitle:
Shri Jitin Prasada Holds High-Level Meetings and Business Interactions to Strengthen India–Hungary Economic and Technological Cooperation

Shri Jitin Prasada Explores Opportunities in Electronics Manufacturing and Engages with Indian Community in Hungary
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 NOV 2026 3:44PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Minister of State for Commerce and Industry, and Electronics and Information Technology, Shri Jitin Prasada, visited Hungary from November 4–6, 2026. The visit reflected the growing momentum in bilateral engagement between India and Hungary and provided an opportunity to further strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, technology, innovation and industrial development.
During the visit, Shri Jitin Prasada called on the Deputy Speaker of the Hungarian National Assembly. The interaction focused on strengthening bilateral relations and exploring opportunities for enhanced cooperation between India and Hungary, including in the broader context of India–European Union relations.
Shri Prasada also met the Minister of Science and Technology of Hungary. The discussions focused on expanding bilateral cooperation in emerging technologies, research and innovation, and exploring opportunities for greater collaboration between industries and research institutions of the two countries.
As part of his institutional engagements, Shri Prasada visited the Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences (MATE), one of Central Europe’s leading agricultural research and educational institutions. The visit provided an opportunity to explore potential cooperation in agricultural research, agri-technology, innovation and sustainable agricultural practices.
Shri Prasada also visited Gedeon Richter Plc., a leading Hungarian pharmaceutical company with an established manufacturing presence in India through Richter Themis Medicare (India) Pvt. Ltd. The visit highlighted existing industrial linkages between the two countries and opportunities for further collaboration in pharmaceutical manufacturing, research and development and healthcare technologies.
On November 5, Shri Jitin Prasada addressed the India–Hungary Business Seminar in Budapest, attended by more than 100 business representatives. Addressing the gathering, the Minister highlighted the significant potential for expanding bilateral trade and investment and called upon Indian and Hungarian companies to explore new business opportunities, forge stronger partnerships and deepen industrial cooperation. He emphasised opportunities in emerging technologies, electronics manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, agriculture and other sectors of mutual interest. The Minister also highlighted the opportunities arising from closer India–European Union economic engagement and encouraged businesses from both countries to strengthen commercial linkages and explore new avenues for cooperation.
As part of his industry engagements, Shri Prasada visited Foxconn’s manufacturing operations in Hungary, engaged in the production of advanced data centre infrastructure, network communication equipment and AI server technologies. The visit highlighted opportunities for strengthening cooperation in electronics manufacturing, digital infrastructure and emerging technologies, including the development of resilient supply chains.
During the visit, Shri Prasada also interacted with members of the Indian community in Hungary at the Amrita Sher-Gil Cultural Centre in Budapest. Addressing the gathering, the Minister acknowledged the contribution of the Indian diaspora in strengthening people-to-people ties and fostering closer relations between India and Hungary.
The visit reaffirmed India’s commitment to strengthening its economic and technological partnership with Hungary. It provided further impetus to bilateral cooperation in trade, investment, innovation and industrial development, while contributing to the broader objective of deepening the India–European Union partnership.
The Indian business delegation accompanying the Shri Prasada participated in a Business Seminar organized by the Embassy of India, during which it interacted with representatives of the Hungarian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (HCCI), Hungarian Export Promotion Agency (HEPA), and Hungarian Investment Promotion Agency (HIPA). As part of the seminar, B2B meetings were also held between Indian companies and their Hungarian counterparts to explore potential business opportunities, strengthen commercial linkages, and identify avenues for enhanced bilateral trade, investment, and business cooperation between India and Hungary.

title: Agreement Signed between DBN (Digital Bharat Nidhi) - Department of Telecommunications; Government of Telangana; TRIICL; BSNL & T-Fibre for Implementation of Amended BharatNet Program in Telangana
subtitle:
₹3,189 Crore Financial Support Approved for Rollout of Amended BharatNet Program in the state of Telangana

Amended BharatNet Program in Telangana to Cover 12,769 Gram Panchayats

Partnership to Strengthen and Upgrade Rural Telecom Infrastructure across Telangana
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 NOV 2026 5:28PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a significant step towards strengthening digital infrastructure and accelerating broadband connectivity across rural Telangana, Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN) under Department of Telecommunications (DoT) signed an Agreement for implementation of the Amended BharatNet Program (ABP) in the State under the State-led model today at Sanchar Bhawan, New Delhi.
The Agreement was signed between Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN), DoT; Government of Telangana; Telangana Rural Internet Infrastructure Corporation Limited (TRIICL); Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) and Telangana Fiber Grid Corporation Limited (T-Fiber) for implementation of the Amended BharatNet Program in the State of Telangana.
The Agreement signing ceremony was held in the august presence of Shri Shyamal Misra, Administrator, Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN). The ceremony was also attended by Shri Anudeep Durishetty, Jt. Secretary, IT E&C Department, Government of Telangana; Shri Papa Sudhakara Rao, Director (Enterprise Business - EB), Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL); Shri Dinesh Kumar Garg, DDG (ABP Implementation-I), Department of Telecommunications; Shri Venu Prasad Panneeru, Telangana Fiber Grid Corporation Limited (T-Fiber) & CEO, Telangana Rural Internet Infrastructure Corporation Limited (TRIICL) and  along with senior officers of DoT, DBN and BSNL.
The signing of the Agreement marks an important milestone towards expeditious implementation of the Program and reflects the shared commitment of the Central Government and the Government of Telangana towards strengthening rural digital infrastructure, enhancing last-mile connectivity and promoting inclusive digital growth.
The Union Cabinet had approved the Amended BharatNet Program on 4th August 2023 with the objective of upgrading, consolidating and expanding the existing BharatNet network to ensure robust and future-ready broadband connectivity to all Gram Panchayats and villages on demand basis.
Under the Amended BharatNet Program in Telangana, the project will be implemented through Telangana Rural Internet Infrastructure Corporation Limited (TRIICL). The Program will have a total scope of 12,769 Gram Panchayats, which includes upgradation of 1,946 Phase I Gram Panchayats from linear to ring topology to enhance network resilience, coverage of 10,787 Phase II Gram Panchayats, and inclusion of 36 newly created Gram Panchayats.
The Government of India has approved financial support of ₹3,189 crores for implementation of the Program in Telangana. The initiative is expected to facilitate around three lakh rural home fibre connections with subsidy support from the Government of India and significantly enhance delivery of digital services including e-Governance, online education, telemedicine, digital payments and citizen-centric services across rural and remote areas of the State.
The Agreement signed today is expected to accelerate execution of the Program in Telangana and further advance the vision of a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.
About Digital Bharat Nidhi
Digital Bharat Nidhi (erstwhile USOF) was established under the Indian Telegraph (Amendment) Act, 2003 w.e.f. 01.04.2002. As per ‘The Telecommunications Act, 2023’ the Universal Service Obligation Fund, has become the Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN). The DBN has mandate to support universal service through promoting access and delivery of telecommunication service in underserved rural, remote and urban areas. It is an attached office of the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications.
In order to achieve objectives of DBN, it covers various schemes and projects including BharatNet, 4G Saturation Project, Provision of Mobile Service in uncovered areas of Aspirational Districts, Mobile Services in Left Wing Extremist Areas, Mobile Services in Himalayan and Border areas, Mobile Services in Islands and Mobile Services in North Eastern Areas.

title: TRAI releases “The Register of Interconnect Agreements (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026”
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 NOV 2026 2:22PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) today released
“The Register of Interconnect Agreements (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026”
. These regulations will take effect from 1st January 2027.
Interconnection in telecommunications refers to the commercial and technical arrangements that connect two or more telecommunications networks, allowing telecommunications traffic to flow between them and enabling users of different service providers to communicate seamlessly. The Register of Interconnect Agreements Regulations, 1999 provide the regulatory framework for the registration and maintenance of interconnect agreements entered into between service providers.
Sub-sections (vii) and (viii) of section 11(1)(b) of the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997 empower,
inter alia
, TRAI to maintain a register of interconnect agreements and make it available for public inspection, subject to the payment of the prescribed fee and fulfilment of other specified requirements.
To ensure that the existing regulatory framework governing interconnection matters remains relevant, transparent, and conducive to efficient interconnection between service providers, TRAI initiated the review of the regulatory framework through a Pre-Consultation Paper on the “Review of the existing TRAI Regulations on Interconnection matters”, dated 03.04.2025. Through this Pre-Consultation Paper, stakeholders’ comments were sought to review,
inter alia
, the Register of Interconnect Agreements Regulations, 1999.
Subsequently, a Consultation Paper on the “Review of the existing TRAI Regulations on Interconnection matters”, providing the background information and taking into account the stakeholders’ comments received during the pre-consultation process, was issued on 10.11.2025. Through the Consultation Paper, the stakeholders’ comments were sought to review,
inter alia
, the Register of Interconnect Agreements Regulations, 1999. After extension, the last dates for furnishing written comments and counter-comments were 15.12.2025 and 29.12.2025, respectively.
In response to the issues raised in the Consultation Paper, seventeen stakeholders submitted their comments, while nine stakeholders submitted counter-comments. As part of the consultation process, an Open House Discussion (OHD) on the Consultation Paper was held on 28.01.2026. Considering the comments received from stakeholders during the consultation process, and their analysis, TRAI has finalised the Register of Interconnect Agreements (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026.
The salient points of the amendment regulations are given below:
Online registration of interconnect agreements
: The amendment regulations provide for all service providers to register their interconnect agreements, as well as any modifications thereto, through the portal established by TRAI for this purpose. The earlier requirement of furnishing printed copies along with a soft copy on floppy/diskette has been dispensed with. Agreements in force as on 1st January 2027 are required to be submitted within fifteen days from that date, and new agreements and modifications within fifteen days of their execution or modification. This will facilitate efficient registration, maintenance of an updated register, and retrieval of interconnect agreements.
Submission of text-searchable electronic documents
: Service providers are required to furnish electronic copies of interconnect agreements and modifications thereto in text-searchable PDF format within the timeline specified for registration. This will facilitate efficient processing, examination, maintenance and retrieval of documents.
Online access to the Register of Interconnect Agreements
: The amended framework enables submission of applications for inspection of the Register of Interconnect Agreements, access to the prescribed part of the Register, and obtaining copies or extracts thereof through the portal. This will facilitate electronic access to the relevant portions of the Register in addition to the existing physical mode, thereby improving accessibility and convenience for members of the public, subject to the applicable regulatory provisions.
Time-bound furnishing of disaggregated information
: TRAI may specify formats for obtaining disaggregated information that can be included in the Register of Interconnect Agreements within the period specified by TRAI. This will ensure timely availability of structured and standardised information, facilitating effective regulatory oversight and greater transparency in interconnection arrangements.
Revision of fees for inspection and copies
: The fee for inspection of the Register has been revised to ₹1,500 per hour or part thereof, and the charge for copies or extracts to ₹500 per page. The revised fee structure is broadly aligned with the framework prescribed under the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (Access to Information) Regulation, 2005.
Graded framework for financial disincentives
: For effective implementation of the regulations, a graded financial disincentive framework has been prescribed for contravention of provisions of these regulations. This will make the enforcement of the regulatory framework more effective, proportionate and commensurate with the nature and seriousness of the contraventions to the provisions of these regulations.
The amendment regulations modernise the framework governing the registration and maintenance of interconnect agreements through digitalisation of the registration, submission and access processes. The provisions relating to time-bound furnishing of information and graded financial disincentives will facilitate effective regulatory oversight and compliance. Overall, the amended framework is expected to enhance administrative efficiency, transparency, accessibility and regulatory certainty in matters relating to interconnect agreements.
The full text of “The Register of Interconnect Agreements (Fourth Amendment) Regulations, 2026”, along with the Explanatory Memorandum, is available on TRAI’s website at
www.trai.gov.in
.

title: Government doubles OMSS (D) rice sale target from 25 LMT to 50 LMT for 2026-27; 25 LMT already sold through e-auctions up to 31 October 2026
subtitle:
Stock disclosure made mandatory for all rice and paddy stocking entities across the country; stock positions to be updated every Friday

Additional allocation of Bharat Rice to NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar to expand availability, particularly in Southern States

Concurrence conveyed to five Southern States to impose stock limits on rice and paddy, wherever necessary, until 31 January 2027
ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 NOV 2026 4:41PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Government of India is closely
monitoring food grain prices
, particularly rice, and undertaking a series of policy interventions to ensure adequate domestic supplies, maintain price stability, prevent hoarding and safeguard consumer interests. In this regard, the Government has undertaken the following measures:
Mandatory Disclosure of Rice and Paddy Stocks Across the Country
The Government of India has issued an order dated 06.11.2026, directing all Traders/Wholesalers, Retailers, Big Chain Retailers and Processors/Millers across all States and Union Territories to declare their stock positions of rice and paddy under the following six categories:
(i) Basmati Rice;
(ii) Non-Basmati Premium Rice;
(iii) non-Basmati Rice;
(iv) Parboiled Rice;
(v) Broken Rice; and
(vi) Paddy.
All entities stocking rice and paddy are required to disclose their stock positions every Friday on the Food Stock Portal (
https://foodstock.dfpd.gov.in
) and ensure that the information furnished is accurate and regularly updated. Any entity found unregistered on the portal or violating the prescribed stock limits shall be liable for appropriate punitive action under Sections 6 and 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.
Concurrence to Southern States for Imposition of Stock Limits
With a view to ensuring the availability of rice to consumers at reasonable prices, particularly in the Southern States, the Government of India has conveyed its concurrence, vide communication dated 06.11.2026, to the State Governments of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana to impose stock limits on paddy and rice through appropriate control orders, wherever considered necessary.
These stock limits shall remain in force up to 31st January 2027. The Central and State Governments will closely monitor the implementation of these measures to ensure adequate market availability and prevent hoarding and black marketing.
Additional Allocation of Bharat Rice to Expand Market Availability
The Government of India is allocating additional quantities of ‘Bharat Rice’ to three agencies,
NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar
with the objective of substantially expanding its sale and availability across the country, particularly in the Southern States. The agencies have also been directed to explore all possible distribution channels to ensure wider reach and easy accessibility of
‘Bharat Rice’
to consumers. The initiative is expected to augment market supplies, improve consumer access to rice at affordable prices and contribute to moderating retail prices.
Doubling of Rice Sale Target Under OMSS (D) for 2026-27
The Government of India has doubled the target quantity of rice for sale through e-auction under the Open Market Sale Scheme (Domestic) [OMSS (D)] for 2026-27, increasing it from 25 LMT to 50 Maturing FY 2026-27 (up to 31.10.2026), a total of 25 LMT of rice has been sold to private parties through OMSS (D) e-auctions, as against 11 LMT during the corresponding period of the previous financial year. This reflects a significant increase in market supplies through the intervention.
These measures reaffirm the Government's commitment to ensuring adequate availability of essential food commodities, maintaining price stability and safeguarding consumer interests across the country.

title: More Than 21,000 Devotees Pay Homage to Sacred Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha at Tawang Monastery
subtitle: Exposition at Tawang Monastery to remain open to the public until November 7, 2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 NOV 2026 9:55AM by PIB Delhi
content:
More than 21,000 devotees have visited Gaden Namgyal Lhatse (Tawang Monastery) so far to offer prayers and pay homage to the sacred relics of Shakyamuni Buddha. Devotees from Tawang and neighbouring regions of Arunachal Pradesh have been gathering at the monastery to seek blessings in the presence of the sacred relics. The exposition at Tawang Monastery will remain open to the public until November 7, 2026.
The exposition holds special historical and spiritual significance as the sacred relics have returned to Arunachal Pradesh after a gap of 13 years. Brought from the National Museum, New Delhi, the relics offer Buddhist monks, nuns, devotees and the general public an opportunity to pay homage to the sacred remains of Shakyamuni Buddha and deepen their engagement with India's rich Buddhist heritage.
The sacred relics were discovered at Piprahwah in Uttar Pradesh in 1898. Their discovery marked an important milestone in the archaeological history of Buddhism. Preserved at the National Museum, New Delhi, the relics hold immense historical, archaeological and spiritual significance for Buddhist communities.
Two special exhibitions have also been organised at Tawang Monastery to highlight the rich legacy of Buddhism. ‘Unearthing the Sacred Piprahwa: The Story of the Holy Buddha Relics and Their Discovery’ by International Buddhist Confederation (IBC) traces the discovery and historical significance of the relics. ‘Crossroads of Dhamma: Classical Legacies, Living Art, and Anthropological Perspectives’, curated by the National Museum, New Delhi, showcases the historical, artistic and cultural dimensions of Buddhism.
Following the exposition at Tawang Monastery, the sacred relics will be taken to TGL Monastery (Lower Gompa), Bomdilla, from November 8 to 13, 2026, and thereafter to the Golden Pagoda, Namsai, from November 14 to 20, 2026. The Holi relics are scheduled to return to the National Museum, New Delhi, on November 21, 2026.
The exposition is being organized by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India in collaboration with the International Buddhist Confederation and the Government of Arunachal Pradesh. The initiative reflects the Government of India's commitment to preserving and promoting the country's rich Buddhist heritage and disseminating the timeless teachings of Bhagwan Buddha, centred on peace, compassion, wisdom and universal brotherhood.

Minimising Pendency and Enhancing Efficiency in Official Work
The Department and its autonomous bodies focused on minimising pendency in official work, reviewing files across various categories, weeding out obsolete files and strengthening record management practices. Waste to Wonde
r

title: Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw Launches Semicon 2.0 Web Application Portal and  Announces 12 Approved Applicants under Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme

content:
Marking another significant step towards strengthening India's semiconductor and electronics ecosystem, Union Minister for Railways, Information & Broadcasting, and Electronics & Information Technology, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw today launched
“Semicon 2.0 – Web Application Portal under the Semicon India Programme”
for Pillars 2, 3 and 4,
followed by the announcement of
12 Approved Applicants under the
Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS)
.
Government of India has been undertaking concerted efforts towards the establishment of a robust and resilient semiconductor ecosystem in the country through various strategic initiatives and policy interventions.
Within a span of few years from its establishment, ISM has catalysed the growth of India’s semiconductor ecosystem, with successful implementation of the first phase of Semicon India Programme (Semicon 1.0), 12 projects were approved across six states, with cumulative investment of over Rs.1.64 lakh crore. Out of twelve, 05 projects have already commenced commercial production as of October 2026.
Also, 105 startups have been provided access to EDA tools, 24 startups are supported through funding, and 15 startups having received venture capital funding. 332 institutions provided with EDA tools under the Chips to Startup (C2S) Programme, with approx. 70,000 students trained so far frame it well.
Union Cabinet has approved Semicon 2.0 with a fiscal outlay of ₹1,27,500 crore under the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM). Marking the next phase of India's semiconductor journey, Semicon 2.0 is focused on six strategic pillars:
Pillar 1:
Design of Chips
Pillar 2:
Machines and Materials
Pillar 3:
Setting up More Fabs
Pillar 4:
Further Strengthening the ATMP/OSAT Industry
Pillar 5:
Research & Development
Pillar 6:
Talent Development
With the launch of the Semicon 2.0 Web Application Portal, applications are now live for Pillar 2, 3 & 4.
Addressing the gathering, Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology, Railways and Information & Broadcasting, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, said that India’s electronics manufacturing journey has moved beyond assembly towards the development of a comprehensive domestic value chain encompassing modules, components, materials and advanced technologies. He highlighted the growing capabilities in battery cells, copper foils, copper-clad laminates and high-end printed circuit boards, noting that government initiatives are strengthening domestic supply chains and creating opportunities for MSMEs, with nearly 50% of the units approved under the scheme belonging to the MSME sector. He emphasised that Semicon India 2.0 would focus on building a robust semiconductor ecosystem, particularly in equipment, materials, chemicals and gases, with a target of attracting at least three major equipment manufacturers and five chemicals and gases companies to India. Calling for rigorous selection of projects, he stressed that quality, technological depth, R&D and global competitiveness must guide the country’s semiconductor ambitions, in line with the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat. He also urged industry stakeholders to collaborate, share expertise and pursue continuous improvement to establish India as a globally competitive electronics and semiconductor manufacturing hub.
In continuation to the approvals of 106 applications involving investment of Rs 69,548 crore announced earlier, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has further approved 12 applications under the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS), with projected investment of Rs 7,503 crore.
The current approvals entail projected production of Rs 39,045 crore and are expected to generate 7,127 direct employment opportunities.
The current approvals cover manufacturing of 10 target segment products, spanning bare components, supply chain products and capital goods. These include:
4 components:
Multi-layer PCB, Relays, Heat Sinks and Specialty Ceramics;
5 supply chain products:
Copper Foil, Anode Material, Cathode Active Material, Polypropylene Film and Camera Rim; and
Capital Goods
and their parts
The approved projects are spread across 7 States viz. Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Punjab, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh, further expanding the geographical footprint of electronics component manufacturing in the country.
The current approvals include 1st time approvals under ECMS for Copper Foil, Cathode Active Material and Specialty Ceramics, further broadening the range of electronics components and upstream materials to be manufactured domestically.
In the components category, approvals for manufacturing have been granted as below:
Multi-layer PCB to
NeST ICELR Private Limited;
Relays to
TDConnex (Chennai) Private Limited
;
Heat Sinks to
Modern Automotives Limited
; and
Specialty Ceramics to
Voltix Semicon Private Limited
.
Further, to strengthen the electronics manufacturing supply chain, approvals have also been granted for manufacturing various supply chain products as below:
Copper Foil, an important input for Copper Clad Laminate (CCL) for PCBs and Li-ion cells, to
Indo Asia Copper Limited
;
Anode Material for Li-ion cells, to
TACC Limited
;
Cathode Active Material to
Vidyuta Materials Private Limited
;
Polypropylene Film, for capacitor-grade dielectric film to
Enerfolie LLP
; and
Camera Rim to
Surface Modification Technologies Pvt. Ltd.
Furthermore, the current approvals continue the emphasis on developing domestic manufacturing capability in capital goods and their parts. Approvals have been granted to
TDConnex (Chennai) Private Limited
for precision molds and tooling;
Rockwell Automation India Private Limited
for power and control systems for capital equipment; and
Wipro Pari Robotics Private Limited
for capital equipment for factory automation and system integration.
With these approvals, overall, 118 applications covering 34 products across 16 States have been approved under ECMS, amounting to expected investment of Rs 77,051 crore, projected production of Rs 5,73,146 crore and expected direct employment for 81,755 persons.
These approvals will strengthen domestic supply chains, deepen value addition, reduce import dependence, and build advanced manufacturing capabilities, further advancing India’s emergence as a global electronics manufacturing hub.
While addressing the media, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, said “India has undergone a fundamental transformation over the past decade. However, this is just the beginning, with various policy initiatives and concerted efforts by the public and private sectors laying the foundation for the growth of the semiconductor and electronics industry and the vision of an Atmanirbhar Bharat”. India is strengthening its domestic electronics manufacturing ecosystem, with a growing focus on manufacturing computers and their components within the country, reducing import dependence and building a robust, self-reliant electronics value chain.
The
Launch of the Semicon 2.0 Web Application Portal
and the
Announcement of Approved Applicants under ECMS
mark a significant step towards strengthening India's semiconductor design and manufacturing capabilities.

title: Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) celebrates 77th Foundation Day and reaffirms India's vision for a “Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat”, through intensified enforcement, digital governance, and mission "Yuva Raksha"
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 NOV 2026 8:22PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Marking its historic
Foundation Day
, the
Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN)
celebrated its 77th foundation Day on 6th November 2026. On this occasion a programme was organised at CBN Headquarters Gwalior in which all the officers and staff participated.
Image: 77th CBN foundation Day celebration programme organised at CBN Headquarters Gwalior.
Deputy Narcotics Commissioner on welcome remarks said that Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN), is a premier and the oldest agency working in the field of Drug Law Enforcement under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance, regulating Licit Cultivation of Opium Poppy, Overseeing Import and Export of Narcotic Drugs, Psychotropic Substances and Precursor Chemicals, and undertaking intelligence-driven enforcement operations to prevent trafficking of contrabands which falls under NDPS Act 1985.
Underlining the Government of India's zero-tolerance policy against drug trafficking and aligning with the vision of a
‘
Drug-Free Youth for a Developed India
’
, the Bureau has significantly scaled up its operational footprint. Originally established on
November 6, 1950, to unify regional opium administrations,
CBN has evolved into a premier National Law Enforcement Powerhouse and India's Competent National Authority (CNA) under United Nations Conventions.
On this Special occasion, CBN also unveiled its Hindi Magazine-
‘
संयम
2.0
’
.
Image: Group Photo on CBN Raising day on which CBN also unveiled its Hindi Magazine-
‘
संयम
2.0
’
.
CBN at Glance:
1. SEVENTY-SIX YEARS OF CHRONOLOGICAL EVOLUTION
From its roots in the
All-India Narcotics Board
created on April 2, 1949, the
unified Opium Department
was formally centralized into the Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) on November 6, 1950 with its Headquarters at Shimla. To place leadership directly alongside the core traditional poppy-growing belts and to effectively monitor the same, the headquarters was permanently relocated from Shimla to Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, in 1960. The enactment of the landmark Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985, completely modernized the agency, converting the CBN from a regulatory administrative department into a multi-role national law enforcement, facilitator and regulatory agency.
2. DISMANTLING TRANSNATIONAL SYNTHETIC DRUG SYNDICATES
From 2022 through October 2026, the CBN's specialized Preventive and Intelligence (P&I) Cells mounted an effective enforcement campaign, booking over 1,000 cases and arresting 1,325 individuals.
Historic Pharmaceutical Diversion Bust:
Highlighting this multi-year crackdown, the CBN executed a monumental seizure in Delhi in July 2026, intercepting
12 crore (120 million) Tramadol Hydrochloride tablets
(250 mg) weighing approximately 100 metric tons, permanently dismantling a major international pharmaceutical smuggling ring.
Environmentally Safe Disposal & Reclamation:
CBN successfully destructed/ incinerated Total 342 Metric tonnes (3,42,000 kg) of seized narcotics, psychotropics and controlled substances. Concurrently, 2535 kg of highly pure raw opium seized from illegal channels was transferred to the Government Opium and Alkaloid Works (GOAW) facility in Neemuch to be reclaimed as vital medicinal alkaloids.
3. SOURCE-LEVEL ELIMINATION: ILLICIT CROP DESTRUCTION DRIVES
From 2022 to October 2026,
Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN) mapped and eradicated huge volume of illegal crops directly at the source. CBN has destructed more than
1,11,300 Acres of illicit cultivation of opium and cannabis
across high-risk states including Himachal Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur and Uttarakhand.
Operation Parivartan (Himachal Pradesh):
In the rugged, high-altitude terrains of the Kullu district, CBN units trekked up to 3,500 meters (11,000 feet) to manually uproot
2,070 hectares (5,165 acres) of illicit cannabis
, by way of blending ground teams with drone technology and precise technological mapping.
Opium Poppy Destruction (Arunachal Pradesh):
Deploying into remote mountain corridors alongside forest and paramilitary forces, the CBN mapped and manually destroyed
3,600 hectares (8,896 acres) of illegal opium poppy fields
during the crop's critical flowering season.
Alternative Development Strategy & "Jan Samvad":
Paired with enforcement, the CBN hosted public town-hall dialogues (
Jan Samvad
) in isolated villages like Malana, for transition farmers into legal, sustainable livelihoods like apiculture, dairy production, animal husbandry, and eco-tourism.
4. MISSION "YUVA RAKSHA": SAFEGUARDING INDIA'S YOUTH
Marking a major transition toward combining statutory enforcement with grassroots social interventions, the CBN
’
s flagship initiative—
Mission "Yuva Raksha"
and CBN outreach initiatives empowered and educated
over 20,000 participants across Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, and Delhi during the 2026 calendar year
.

title: National Exercise ‘VAJRA-SAT’ Concludes at Bengaluru, Strengthening India's Preparedness for Foot-and-Mouth Disease
subtitle: Two-day exercise brings together 83 participants from 25 States, three Union Territories and key national institutions to strengthen surveillance, early detection and coordinated response
ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 NOV 2026 12:56PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Government of India, in coordination with ICAR-National Institute of Veterinary Epidemiology and Disease Informatics (ICAR-NIVEDI), Bengaluru, organised the two-day National Tabletop Exercise
‘VAJRA-SAT’ on Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD) serotype SAT-1 preparedness
on 4–5 November 2026. The exercise, held under the theme
“Detect Early, Confirm Fast, Contain Together,”
concluded today with recommendations aimed at strengthening national preparedness and coordinated response to transboundary animal diseases.
FMD serotype SAT-1 has not been reported in India.
In view of its geographical spread beyond Africa to parts of West Asia, the exercise was undertaken as a proactive preparedness initiative to safeguard livestock health, farmers' livelihoods and the livestock economy.
The exercise brought together
83 participants from 25 States, three Union Territories and key national institutions
, including State Animal Husbandry Departments, ICAR institutions, veterinary diagnostic laboratories, veterinary universities, vaccine manufacturers, and defence and border guarding agencies. Through simulated outbreak scenarios, participants deliberated on early detection, laboratory confirmation, epidemiological investigation, animal movement control, emergency vaccination preparedness, risk communication and coordinated response.
The exercise was inaugurated on 4 November by
Dr. Naveena B.M., Animal Husbandry Commissioner, DAHD
, who emphasised the importance of advance preparedness, early disease detection, timely response and effective coordination among Central and State agencies.
Dr. Baldev R. Gulati, Director, ICAR-NIVEDI
, highlighted the evolving epidemiological situation of FMD SAT-1 and the importance of risk-based surveillance, epidemiological intelligence and early warning systems.
Dr. J.K. Mohapatra, Director, ICAR-National Institute of Foot-and-Mouth Disease (ICAR-NIFMD)
, emphasised the importance of laboratory preparedness, rapid diagnosis and vaccine readiness.
Brigadier M.M. Ramachandra, Director, National Security Council Secretariat
, highlighted the importance of inter-agency coordination and border vigilance in preventing transboundary animal diseases.
The concluding session on 5 November was chaired by
Shri Rama Shankar Sinha, Additional Secretary (Livestock Health), DAHD
, who emphasised the importance of strengthening national and State-level preparedness and enhancing laboratory diagnostic capacity, including regional FMD laboratories and Regional Disease Diagnostic Laboratories (RDDLs), with technical support from ICAR-NIFMD.
During the concluding deliberations, participants highlighted the importance of timely reporting, rapid laboratory confirmation, disease surveillance, movement control, vaccine preparedness and inter-State coordination. The exercise provided valuable inputs for developing appropriate preparedness and response strategies for FMD SAT-1. The observations and recommendations emerging from the exercise will further support national preparedness and coordinated response mechanisms.
A separate technical meeting on FMD-free compartmentalisation was also held on 5 November 2026, under the co-chairmanship of the Additional Secretary (LH) and the Animal Husbandry Commissioner, with participation from States. The discussions focused on FMD-free compartmentalisation of semen production centres and semen banks. The initiative aims to strengthen disease prevention, safeguard valuable livestock genetic resources and facilitate safe livestock trade.

title: Hon’ble Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh Releases Publication Titled “Minimum Standard Protocol for Semen Production and Standard Operating Procedures for Artificial Insemination using Liquid Semen in Pigs” to Accelerate Genetic Improvement and Enhance Livelihoods, Especially in North-East India
ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 NOV 2026 7:17AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Publication to strengthen scientific pig breeding across the North-Eastern Region
Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, Hon’ble Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, released the publication titled
“Minimum Standard Protocol for Semen Production and Standard Operating Procedures for Artificial Insemination using Liquid Semen in Pigs”
on 2 November 2026, during his two-day visit to Sikkim. This initiative aims to promote scientific pig breeding, facilitate genetic improvement and enhance livelihood opportunities for pig farmers, particularly in the North-Eastern Region (NER).
The newly released protocol provides a comprehensive framework for scientific semen production, quality assurance, biosecurity, semen preservation, transportation, and artificial insemination practices in pigs. The document lays down standardized procedures for establishing and operating pig semen production laboratories and for delivering efficient artificial insemination services across the states in the country.
India has a pig population of 9.06 million as per the 20th Livestock Census (2019), accounting for 1.7% of the country's total livestock population. While pigs are reared across all agro-climatic regions, the North-Eastern Region remains the heartland of pig farming in India, contributing nearly 45% of the national pig population. Indigenous and non-descript pigs constitute about 79% of the total pig population, highlighting the significant scope for genetic improvement through scientific breeding interventions. Strengthening access to quality germplasm, improved breeding technologies and artificial insemination services is therefore critical for enhancing productivity, increasing pork production and improving the livelihoods of smallholder pig farmers, particularly across the North-Eastern states.
The key features and expected outcomes of the protocol are as follows:
The protocol would serve as a practical guide for States, veterinarians, breeding centres and farmers to facilitate the wider adoption of artificial insemination and modern breeding practices.
The initiative is expected to improve reproductive efficiency, accelerate genetic improvement and support the conservation and upgrading of indigenous pig germplasm prevalent in the North-East.
The publication also covers the entire pig artificial insemination value chain, including:
Breeding boar selection
Semen collection, evaluation, processing, storage and transportation
Laboratory quality management
Disease prevention and biosecurity measures
Its implementation is expected to enhance the availability of superior breeding material and improve the productivity and profitability of pig farming enterprises.
The initiative is expected to contribute significantly to increase pork production, livelihood generation and sustainable growth of the pig sector in the region.

title: Union Health Ministry Reviews Progress of AB PM-JAY and ABDM with States and UTs; Charts Roadmap for Strengthening Implementation
subtitle:
Every Rupee Spent on Healthcare Must Lead to Better Care for Our People: Dr. Sunil Kumar Barnwal, CEO, NHA

Focus Must Shift from Financing Treatment to Achieving Better Health Outcomes: CEO, NHA

4.2 Crore Beneficiaries Enrolled and 2.2 Lakh People Treated under AB PM-JAY in West Bengal Since Its Launch: Shri Manoj Kumar Aggarwal, Chief Secretary, Government of West Bengal

Two-day National Review Meeting focuses on strengthening beneficiary coverage, healthcare delivery, financial protection and digital health integration
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 NOV 2026 4:34PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Health Authority (NHA), under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, convened a two-day National Review Meeting in Kolkata on 5–6 November 2026 to review the progress of Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) and the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM), and to deliberate on priorities and strategies for strengthening their implementation in the coming phase.
The meeting brought together senior officials from States and Union Territories to review the implementation and progress of Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) and the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM), and to deliberate on priorities and strategies for strengthening these flagship initiatives in the coming years.
The meeting provided a platform for the Centre and States to assess programme performance, share implementation experiences and identify measures to improve the reach, efficiency and impact of the two initiatives. The deliberations focused on expanding beneficiary coverage, strengthening healthcare delivery, ensuring financial protection and accelerating digital health adoption. Particular emphasis was placed on leveraging technology, data analytics, automation and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to enhance operational efficiency, transparency, accountability and health outcomes.
Addressing the gathering, Dr. Sunil Kumar Barnwal, Chief Executive Officer, National Health Authority, highlighted the progress made by West Bengal following its integration with the national AB PM-JAY platform, with over four crore Ayushman Cards generated within a short span. He emphasised that the next phase of implementation must focus on translating the achievements in coverage into improved access to quality healthcare and better health outcomes for beneficiaries.
“Every rupee spent on healthcare must lead to better care for our people. Technology, data and artificial intelligence can strengthen implementation, improve efficiency and support more informed decision-making. As we move forward, our focus must increasingly shift from financing treatment towards achieving better health outcomes for beneficiaries,” he said.
Speaking at the Occasion, Shri Manoj Kumar Aggarwal, Chief Secretary, Government of West Bengal, emphasised the importance of strengthening primary healthcare alongside financial protection under AB PM-JAY. He observed that while the scheme provides financial security to eligible families at the hospitalisation stage, a strong primary healthcare system is essential for preventive care, early detection of diseases and reducing the burden on hospitals.
“Healthcare should never push a family into poverty. AB PM-JAY is a game changer in ensuring healthcare security for every eligible family. At the same time, strengthening primary healthcare is essential to reducing the burden on hospitals and improving health outcomes. West Bengal is committed to making the implementation of the scheme robust, comprehensive and people-centric,” he said.
Shri Narayan Swaroop Nigam, Principal Secretary, Department of Health and Family Welfare, Government of West Bengal, stated that West Bengal joined AB PM-JAY as the 36th State. Since the launch of the scheme in the State on 16 August 2026, 4.2 crore beneficiaries have been enrolled and 2.2 lakh people have received treatment under the scheme. He highlighted that AB PM-JAY and ABDM represent two complementary pillars of healthcare transformation, bringing together financial protection and digital empowerment.
The inaugural session was also attended by Shri Ashish Madhao Rao, Additional CEO, NHA; Shri Kiran Gopal Vaska, Joint Secretary and Mission Director, ABDM; Ms. Varnali Deka, Joint Secretary and Mission Director, ABDM, NHA; and Shri Sharad Dwivedi, CEO, State Health Agency, West Bengal, along with senior officials from NHA and representatives of participating States and Union Territories.
A key focus of the deliberations was the need to ensure that all eligible beneficiaries are covered under AB PM-JAY and are adequately informed about the benefits available under the scheme. The review also examined the progress of ABDM and explored ways to strengthen its adoption across healthcare facilities. Emphasis was placed on coordinated implementation of the two initiatives to facilitate seamless access to healthcare services, improve beneficiary experience and establish a more integrated and patient-centric healthcare ecosystem.
The meeting also deliberated on strengthening claims processing and fraud prevention mechanisms under AB PM-JAY. A dedicated session on the National Anti-Fraud Unit (NAFU) and auto-adjudication examined the increasing use of automation in claims settlement, including its impact on processing timelines, operational costs and the quality of adjudication. The importance of regular fraud reviews, effective monitoring mechanisms and strengthening the institutional capacity of State Anti-Fraud Units was underscored to ensure transparency and accountability in the implementation of the scheme.
Recognising the importance of digital transformation in improving healthcare delivery, the meeting reviewed the Model Digital Health Facility Framework and the implementation experience of Tripura. The discussions highlighted that successful digitisation of healthcare facilities requires not only the deployment of digital solutions but also appropriate changes in institutional processes, workflow redesign and regular capacity building of healthcare personnel. Such integration is expected to strengthen ABDM-enabled workflows while ensuring the availability of accurate and reliable data for effective implementation of AB PM-JAY.
The role of Artificial Intelligence in strengthening healthcare systems was another important area of discussion. Prof. Phaneendra Yalavarthy, TANUH, IISc Bengaluru, presented the Benchmarking Open Data Platform for Health AI (BODH), which enables the evaluation and benchmarking of health AI models using Indian datasets. States were encouraged to utilise the platform to assess the performance and suitability of AI solutions before their adoption and to incorporate BODH-based benchmarking into their healthcare AI procurement processes.
The meeting also reviewed the operationalisation of the National Health Claims Exchange (NHCX), emphasising the importance of ABDM-enabled Hospital Information Systems for its effective integration across AB PM-JAY empanelled hospitals. Greater integration by hospitals and digital solution providers was identified as an important requirement for expediting claims processing and improving the accuracy and quality of claims adjudication.
Further, the Health Analytics and Artificial Intelligence Unit (HAAU) presented its findings on data quality. The discussions highlighted the need to strengthen institutional capacity for data analytics and evidence-based decision-making, with States committing to establish dedicated analytics and AI teams to support informed planning and targeted interventions.
On the second day, the deliberations focused on health financing models, convergence of health schemes, ease of digital integration and cybersecurity. Dr. Darez Ahamed, Secretary, Health and Family Welfare, Government of Tamil Nadu, shared the State's experience in implementing insurance and assurance models of health coverage. The discussion highlighted the importance of aligning the choice of health coverage model with the nature of risks being addressed, supported by ring-fenced funds and timely payments to hospitals.
The session on convergence explored the scope for States to leverage NHA's IT platform for implementing their respective health schemes. The platform's existing health benefit packages, empanelled hospital network and fraud-detection mechanisms were discussed as potential enablers for greater standardisation, streamlined implementation and strengthened monitoring of State health schemes.
A demonstration of Sandbox 2.0, enhanced with agentic AI capabilities, showcased the potential of AI-assisted tools in simplifying and expediting ABDM integration. During the demonstration, an ABDM Milestone 1 integration for ABHA creation was successfully completed in real time, illustrating how AI can significantly reduce the time and technical effort required for integration. The initiative is expected to facilitate faster onboarding of technology partners and Hospital Information System providers, while reducing dependence on manual technical support.
In view of the sensitive nature of information handled by national digital health platforms, cybersecurity was also accorded significant attention. The discussions examined potential threats, including phishing attacks, fraudulent URLs and applications, credential leaks and third-party vulnerabilities. States were advised to designate dedicated cybersecurity leads, strengthen authentication and access controls, and undertake regular security audits of applications and APIs to safeguard digital health infrastructure and ensure the security of health data.
The meeting also witnessed a demonstration of NHA's Ambient AI-enabled Voice Scribe, a technology that converts doctor-patient conversations into structured clinical records in multiple Indian languages. The records are reviewed and approved by doctors before being linked to ABHA. The demonstration highlighted the potential of this technology to reduce the documentation burden on doctors, streamline clinical workflows and accelerate the digitisation of healthcare facilities.
The National Review Meeting concluded with a shared roadmap for the next phase of implementation of AB PM-JAY and ABDM. The deliberations reaffirmed the importance of sustained Centre-State coordination, stronger implementation mechanisms and effective utilisation of technology to translate the progress achieved under the two flagship initiatives into tangible benefits for citizens.
The discussions underscored that the next phase must focus not only on expanding coverage and digital adoption but also on ensuring timely access to quality healthcare, strengthening financial protection and improving health outcomes. Reliable data, secure and interoperable digital systems, robust monitoring mechanisms and the responsible adoption of emerging technologies will remain central to achieving these objectives.
The two-day meeting comprised 15 sessions covering various aspects of programme implementation, operational efficiency, digital health infrastructure and emerging technological interventions.
The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare reiterated their commitment to working collaboratively towards strengthening the implementation of AB PM-JAY and ABDM and advancing the broader vision of an accessible, affordable, efficient and people-centric healthcare system in the country.

content:
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today presented the President’s Colour to the Uttarakhand Police in Dehradun. On this occasion, Uttarakhand Chief Minister Shri Pushkar Singh Dhami, along with several other dignitaries, was present.
Addressing the President’s Colour investiture ceremony, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah congratulated the Uttarakhand Police on receiving the President’s Colour and said that Uttarakhand Police has become the 16th force in the country to receive this highest honour. He said that this is a moment of immense pride for all those jawans and officers who have served in the Uttarakhand Police over the past 25 years since the formation of the state, those currently serving, and those who have retired. Shri Shah said that the Uttarakhand Police jawans and officers have not only adopted the three guiding principles of “Karm Satyam Shauryam” as their ideal, but have also made them the foundation of their lives and duties. It is on the strength of these very values that the Uttarakhand Police has achieved the honour of receiving the President’s Colour in such a short span of time.
Shri Amit Shah said that Devbhoomi Uttarakhand is endowed with natural beauty. Its snow-clad peaks, beautiful lakes, dense forests, elephant safaris, and the origins of Mother Ganga and Yamuna attract tourists from across the world. At the same time, Lord Badrinath himself resides here, Baba Kedarnath protects us, and the two mother goddesses emerging from Gangotri and Yamunotri not only bring prosperity to the lives of crores of people but also elevate them spiritually. Shri Shah said that Hemkund Sahib, described by the tenth Sikh Guru, is a major centre of attraction not only for Sikh devotees but for all pilgrims. Along with so many pilgrimage sites, the responsibility of ensuring the safety of lakhs of pilgrims who visit the prestigious Kumbh Mela, the annual Char Dham Yatra, Hemkund Sahib, and Kainchi Dham rests with the jawans of the Uttarakhand Police.
The Home Minister said that he comes from a state from where the largest number of pilgrims visit Devbhoomi, yet he has never heard any complaint about the Uttarakhand Police from any pilgrim of his state, which is a matter of pride for the state police and for all of us.
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that receiving the President’s Colour is a moment of great pride for any force. He said that today we have all felt this moment with many hopes and aspirations, and with a sense of responsibility to instil confidence of security among the citizens of Uttarakhand and the people coming here from across the country. However, before this moment arrived, 206 brave jawans of the Uttarakhand Police made the supreme sacrifice. Shri Shah said that with moist eyes we not only pay homage to those jawans but also express our gratitude to them. It is on the strength of their dedication, discipline and valour, along with the service, sacrifice, unwavering commitment, continuous devotion to duty, outstanding professionalism and discipline of those currently serving, that the Uttarakhand Police has today become the 16th police force in the country to be awarded the President’s Colour.
Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that the journey of the Uttarakhand Police, which has grown from 13,000 jawans to over 26,000 personnel, has been quite challenging. He said that Uttarakhand has always struggled against various kinds of natural disasters. Major natural calamities have repeatedly forced the state into hardship. Yet, the jawans of the Uttarakhand Police, whether serving as part of the SDRF or as regular police, have resolutely confronted every kind of sudden disaster, from forest fires and landslides to the workers trapped in tunnels. He said that the Uttarakhand Police has handled the burden of a growing population and the continuous movement of lakhs of pilgrims every month with great efficiency. Shri Shah said that if anyone reaches a person stranded in a remote area first, it is either a jawan of the ITBP or of the Uttarakhand Police. It is because of this trust and confidence that crores of devotees find the courage to come here. He said that the Uttarakhand Police displayed indomitable valour during the rescue of workers trapped in the Silkyara tunnel, and several other calamities including those at Dharali, Tharali, Syanchatti and Maldevta.
Shri Amit Shah said that one of the major problems of Uttarakhand is the migration taking place from villages situated on the peaks and in the border areas. He said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has launched the Vibrant Villages Programme to address this issue. Working shoulder to shoulder with the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF), the Uttarakhand Police is also fully dedicated to fulfilling all the standards of this programme. He said that as a result, there are at least 50 villages where, instead of migration, people have started resettling, which is a ray of hope for us.
Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that if the greatest efforts in the country to implement the
Naveen Nyay Sanhitas
(new criminal laws) have been made anywhere, they have been made in Uttarakhand. He assured the people of the state on behalf of the Uttarakhand government that the Uttarakhand Police will complete the process of securing convictions for the accused in any FIR registered after May 2027 within three years. He said that the residents of Devbhoomi will now be free from the endless cycle of dates. Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah addressed the Uttarakhand State Foundation Day celebrations in Dehradun today. On this occasion, Uttarakhand Chief Minister Shri Pushkar Singh Dhami, along with several other distinguished dignitaries, was also present.
Addressing the gathering on this occasion, Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that today is a day to remember and express gratitude to our revered late leader, Atal Bihari Vajpayee. For many years, the people of this region had been struggling for the creation of a separate state of Uttarakhand, but governments led by opposition parties did not allow the state to be formed. Former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee fulfilled this long-standing demand by establishing Uttarakhand on 9 November 2000.
Shri Amit Shah said that while Atal Bihari Vajpayee created Uttarakhand, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has worked towards transforming and developing the state. A developed Uttarakhand is the first milestone in the journey towards a developed India. He said that our government has decided to celebrate Uttarakhand State Foundation Day as an occasion of pride, achievement and resolve. We take pride in the divine land of Uttarakhand and in the decision taken by our revered Atal Bihari Vajpayee to establish the state. We are equally proud of the progress being made towards building a developed Uttarakhand under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and Chief Minister Shri Pushkar Singh Dhami. He further said that we resolve to make Devbhoomi Uttarakhand the first developed state in the journey towards a developed India by 2047.
Union Home Minister said that today is the day to take a pledge to fulfil the dreams of the people and youth of Devbhoomi who have made supreme sacrifices in the service and protection of Bharat Mata. We must resolve to preserve our cultural heritage and the environment of Uttarakhand while transforming the state into a developed state. We must also resolve to inspire the younger generation to follow the path of patriotism and valour.
Shri Amit Shah said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi at the Centre and Chief Minister Shri Pushkar Singh Dhami in Uttarakhand, efforts are being made for the development of the state. Our government has ensured that the development of Uttarakhand continues uninterrupted for the past 10 years. He said that today, in this relatively small state, the foundation stone laying and inauguration of a total of 63 development projects worth ₹1,508 crore have taken place. He further stated that today, 15 individuals will be conferred with the Uttarakhand Gaurav Samman, six individuals will receive the State Bravery Award, and two individuals will be honoured with the Lifetime Achievement Award. These honours symbolise that our government takes pride in recognising and felicitating those who have made significant contributions towards making Uttarakhand a great state.
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that Uttarakhand's Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) has grown by 50% since 2022. While GSDP is an indicator of the growth of a state's economy, the prosperity of its citizens must also grow alongside the state's development. Our government has worked towards increasing the per capita income in Uttarakhand by 40%. He said that the Global Investment Summit attracted investments worth ₹3.56 lakh crore to Uttarakhand. Of this, industrial projects worth ₹1 lakh crore have already been grounded and have commenced operations. Despite the limited time, the relatively small size of the state and several challenges associated with industrial development, Dhami government has successfully translated investments worth ₹1 lakh crore into projects on the ground.
Shri Amit Shah said that Uttarakhand is the first state in the country to have implemented the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) on the ground. He stated that following its implementation, no one in Uttarakhand can now have multiple marriages, and no woman can be subjected to the indignity of triple talaq. He further said that, following Uttarakhand's example, 15 states across the country have now moved forward in the direction of implementing the UCC. He said that Uttarakhand has introduced such a stringent anti-cheating law that courts will now be able to punish those who cheat in examinations, facilitate cheating, or are involved in paper leaks without delay. He added that 35,000 people have been provided government jobs without any recommendations or favouritism. He highlighted several other initiatives, including the Song, Jamrani and Kishau multipurpose dam projects; numerous drinking water, irrigation and energy projects; 30% reservation for women in government jobs; 33% reservation for women in cooperative societies; creation of more than 3 lakh Lakhpati Didis; the Homestay Scheme; 10% reservation for statehood activists; and an increase in the ex-gratia assistance to the families of martyrs from ₹10 lakh to ₹50 lakh. He further stated that the government has established an AIIMS satellite center at Kichha and developed an Industrial Smart City. Under the Vibrant Villages Programme, development works worth ₹270 crore have been undertaken in 51 border villages. Initiatives such as House of Himalayas and the Millet Mission have also been launched to take locally produced Himalayan and traditional hill products to every corner of the country. He said that the opposition governments had undertaken only one task: preventing the formation of Uttarakhand.
Shri Amit Shah said that in the next elections, the people of Uttarakhand must decide whether they want a government led by our party that delivers development or a government led by the opposition party that engages in corruption. He said that for years, the principal opposition party had left Uttarakhand dependent on a money-order economy and migration. It had formulated policies under which the water of the hills never benefited the people of the region. He stated that our government has made every possible effort to curb migration and replace the money-order economy with an industrial economy that generates wealth and creates economic opportunities within the state. He further said that the tourism sector in Uttarakhand has witnessed a growth of 380%.
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that opposition government did not build roads in Uttarakhand, arguing that roads would allow enemies to enter the country. Our government has built roads, and Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has strengthened the country to such an extent that no one now dares to challenge India's borders. He said that whenever anyone attempted to violate India's borders, the Modi government responded by carrying out surgical strikes, air strikes and Operation Sindoor, entering enemy territory and eliminating the threat. He stated that previous opposition governments had kept Uttarakhand deprived of basic infrastructure and facilities out of fear of the enemy. Earlier governments treated border villages as the last villages of the country and left them to their fate. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi transformed these border villages into the country's first villages and launched the Vibrant Villages Programme. Through an investment of ₹270 crore, development initiatives have been undertaken in 51 border villages, encouraging young people to return to these villages.
Shri Amit Shah said that the issue of SIR (Special Intensive Revision) is currently being discussed. He alleged that the Leader of the Opposition's campaign is not a ‘Vote Bachao’ campaign but a ‘Ghuspaithiya Bachao’ campaign. He asked the people of Uttarakhand whether the electoral rolls should be made free of infiltrators and whether every infiltrator should be expelled from Devbhoomi Uttarakhand and India. He said that the false narrative being propagated by the Leader of the Opposition would not be accepted by the people of India. He further alleged that opposition parties were unwilling to abandon their politics of appeasement. He said that they were opposing the construction of the Ram Temple, allowing infiltration and pursuing policies that promoted demographic changes. He added that our party's government had put an end to all these practices. Shri Amit Shah said that over the past 10 years, our party's government had provided corruption-free governance in Uttarakhand. He accused the previous opposition government of being involved in several alleged scandals, including a sting controversy involving a former Chief Minister, allegations that the Secretariat had become a hub for commission agents, SC-ST scholarship scam, the liquor policy sting operation and the Kumaon foodgrain scam. He concluded by saying that our party's government has worked to ensure that every single rupee reaches the people of Devbhoomi Uttarakhand.

To achieve all three objectives, we seek the people's mandate and blessings for a third consecutive term.

title: Face Authentication Adoption Surges to 80% as DLC Campaign 5 Generates Nearly 40 Lakh Certificates in First Five Days: Dr. Jitendra Singh
subtitle:
Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Launches Nationwide DLC Campaign 5 as Digital Life Certificate Generation Surges 60% in First Five Days 

1.17 crore of 1.92 crore DLCs generated through face authentication last year, reflecting growing trust in digital technology, says Dr. Jitendra Singh

Pensioners' experience, expertise and potential vital to Viksit Bharat; Dr. Jitendra Singh advocates synergy between generations for nation-building 

Nationwide campaign to cover nearly 3,000 locations with doorstep services for elderly pensioners unable to visit camps
ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                06 NOV 2026 4:47PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr Jitendra Singh today launched the Nationwide Digital Life Certificate (DLC) Campaign 5, with nearly 40 lakh Digital Life Certificates generated in its first five days against approximately 25 lakh during the corresponding period last year, registering a 60 per cent increase.
Face authentication adoption has surged from 61 per cent to nearly 80 per cent during the same period, reflecting growing confidence among pensioners in technology-enabled pension services. Dr. Jitendra Singh said the overwhelming response demonstrates how digital innovation is transforming pensioners' ease of living while making governance more accessible, convenient and dignified for elderly citizens.
Addressing a press conference at the National Media Centre, New Delhi, Dr Jitendra Singh said the campaign has progressively evolved into a nationwide movement, bringing together government departments, pension disbursing banks, pensioners' associations and families to facilitate seamless pension-related services.
The event was attended by Secretary, Department of Pension & Pensioners’ Welfare, Ms. Nivedita Shukla Verma; Chairman and CEO, Railway Board, Shri Satish Kumar; Secretary, Department of Posts, Shri Subrat Das; Controller General of Defence Accounts, Ms. Alka Nangia Arora; Controller General of Communication Accounts, Ms. Vandana Gupta; CEO, UIDAI, Shri Saurabh Vijay; and Additional Director General, PIB, Shri Nanda Kishore Reddy, among other senior officials.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the fundamental objective of the campaign is to ensure ease of living for elderly citizens, adding that India's changing demographic and socio-economic landscape makes pensioners an increasingly important segment of society. The number of central government pensioners has now reached nearly 70 lakh against approximately 50 lakh working employees, reversing the earlier situation when the number of working employees was around 55–60 lakh and pensioners approximately 50 lakh.
The Minister said increasing life expectancy and improved health conditions have created a new opportunity to harness the experience, expertise and potential of senior citizens for nation-building. Many employees retire at the age of 60 when they are still at the prime of their health, experience and professional capabilities.
In the context of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of Viksit Bharat, Dr. Jitendra Singh said elderly citizens must be actively engaged in nation-building by ensuring their comfort, health and financial security, enabling them to contribute their potential to constructive national endeavours. He emphasised the need to build a healthy synergy between the younger and older generations as partners in India's development journey.
Tracing the evolution of Digital Life Certificates, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the government initially relied on conventional life certificates, followed by biometric authentication through fingerprints, before introducing face authentication technology to address limitations faced by elderly pensioners. He said face recognition technology has emerged as a convenient and accessible solution, enabling pensioners to generate Digital Life Certificates through a mobile phone without the need to visit banks or offices. The Minister said that out of 1.92 crore Digital Life Certificates generated last year, approximately 1.17 crore were through face authentication, demonstrating the growing preference for this technology among pensioners.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said the campaign has increasingly become a “whole of government” and “whole of society” movement, with pensioners' welfare associations and family members playing an active role in facilitating Digital Life Certificates. Grandchildren assisting grandparents in generating DLCs, he said, have made technology adoption an engaging family experience, while familiarising senior citizens with digital tools and services. He said the campaign's growing acceptance reflects the collective participation of government institutions, pensioners and society in advancing citizen-centric governance.
The Minister also referred to several pension-related reforms undertaken by the Department of Pension & Pensioners’ Welfare, including pension adalats for resolution of long-pending cases, a dedicated grievance redressal mechanism through CPENGRAMS, and simplification of obsolete rules and procedures.
He said reforms have focused on removing unnecessary procedural hurdles rather than introducing additional regulations, making pension administration more responsive to citizens' needs. Dr. Jitendra Singh reiterated that the government remains open to suggestions from pensioners wherever they face difficulties, bottlenecks or procedural challenges, and would continue eliminating obsolete rules and conditions to improve their welfare.
Secretary, Department of Pension & Pensioners’ Welfare, Ms. Nivedita Shukla Verma, said the Digital Life Certificate Campaign is being pursued with the objectives of pensioners' welfare, ease of living, digital empowerment and dignity of pensioners, while advancing the government's vision of minimum government and maximum governance.
She said the campaign provides pensioners with a quick, convenient and accessible interface, reducing the need for repeated visits and procedural difficulties. She added that extensive outreach through print and social media, WhatsApp networks, short explanatory videos and pensioners' associations has helped spread awareness and encourage participation.
Ms. Nivedita Shukla Verma said the campaign represents a comprehensive whole-of-government approach, with pension disbursing banks, Ministries of Railways and Defence, Department of Telecommunications, Department of Posts, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, UIDAI, State Governments and pensioners' associations working together. Nearly 3,000 locations are being covered through camps, with special efforts to reach pensioners in remote areas.
Doorstep services have also been arranged for pensioners unable to visit camps, ensuring that the campaign reaches elderly citizens irrespective of mobility or geographical constraints. The Secretary appealed to pensioners to take full advantage of the campaign and encourage fellow pensioners to participate, saying that positive experiences and word-of-mouth communication would further strengthen its reach and impact.
During the programme, a Compendium Booklet was released, along with a Coffee Table e-book documenting Nationwide DLC Campaign 4.0.

19,88,826 cleanliness campaign sites

₹ 970.33 crore

277.82 lakh square feet of office space
was freed for productive utilisation, marking an increase of approximately 19% over the previous campaign.
The campaign also recorded significant progress in minimising pendency and improving administrative efficiency. A total of
9,99,168
public grievances were disposed of, while
40,878
public grievance appeals were addressed. Ministries and Departments reviewed
26,79,875
physical files and weeded out
15,76,828
files. In the digital domain,
9,58,864
e-files were reviewed and
7,01,723
e-files were closed, reinforcing the Government's commitment towards efficient, paperless and citizen- centric administration.

Scientific Management of E-Waste

Through coordinated efforts involving DARPG, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), State Pollution Control Boards and the recycling industry, a structured mechanism was facilitated for connecting Government offices with authorised recyclers, refurbishers and producers.

disposal of e-waste items generated revenue of about ₹50 crore

Whole-of-Government Participation
A distinctive feature of Special Campaign 6 was the introduction of dedicated One- Day Event, wherein selected Ministries and Departments undertook coordinated cleanliness and waste management activities across all their field offices and establishments on a designated day. A total of 27 Ministries/Departments under the Government of India organised these events, covering 2,40,156 field offices.
Creating Public Awareness for the important cause of Cleanliness

Special Campaign- Institutionalizing Swachhata, e-Governance and reducing Pendency
Special Campaign 6 has further reinforced the Government's commitment to institutionalising Swachhata, reducing administrative pendency, promoting scientific waste management and ensuring optimal utilisation of public resources.
The innovative practices adopted by Ministries and Departments provide replicable models for sustainable workplace management and citizen-centric governance.
